7. Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

The LiteLLM package on the Python Package Index (PyPI) was recently compromised, with version 1.107.0 containing malicious code. The backdoor was designed to steal credentials from developers who installed the update. Users are advised to verify their dependencies and rotate any exposed secrets.

My Take

Installing packages from PyPI is basically playing Russian roulette with a blindfold on. One minute you're just trying to get your LLM wrapper to work, the next you're donating your AWS keys to a stranger in a basement. Always pin your versions and pray to the dependency gods.
